title: One system or two: a live session and the unattended runner adding and handling work identically, grounded against the conveyor code, four live probes of claude -p, and controller, merge-queue and ephemeral-runner prior art
summary: Grounds decision #3722 (are the interactive session and the runner one system, or two systems that share operations). Prior art (Kubernetes controllers, merge-queue bots, Temporal and GitHub Actions triggers, ephemeral runners) converges on one reconciler with many callers, where the human writes intent and trigger identity is data. The code read changes the card's framing in four places. (1) Guard bookkeeping is already mostly derived: the build guard has a restart-surviving floor from the agent listing (#3403) and the fix and ci-heal caps from PR comments (#2643, #2666). (2) The durable facts it leans on are the real defect: the queue, the pause marker, run records and completion records all resolve their root from the SCRIPT location, so a hook or session in a lane clone sees different state than the runner. (3) The card's three liveness models are one: the lane lease pid is dormant, the run record stamp is a cache of the agent listing, and every reader shares one function. (4) The card's premise that a session's dispatch is supervised by construction is contradicted by the record (load 28 on 12 cores on 2026-09-19, from hand dispatch) and by the pause marker's own header. Probes of claude -p (CLI 2.1.278) show a run-to-completion launch works on the probed axes: it exits when done, is listed with a pid and its -n name while running, leaves the listing on exit, and resumes by the same session id. It is not a launch flag change, though: the spawn is a blocking call with a 60-second kill, the lease reaper skips any session whose kind is not background, and the worker permission profile under -p is unprobed. The recommended default is the resident model with a completion-record and deadline reaper, and run-to-completion is the named, gated target.
